preview.subject: HANGS Construction Services Q3 2026 payroll reports
preview.body:
Hello,

Please prepare the Q3 2026 payroll reports for HANGS Construction Services LLC: Form 941, the ESD unemployment insurance tax and wage report, the Paid Leave and WA Cares report, and the L&I workers' compensation quarterly report. Each report is a draft for review; nothing is filed or paid until the review is done.

Attached are the Q3 2026 payroll register, the federal tax deposit log and the Q2 2026 year-to-date wages by employee. The register is the final export from the payroll system for the six Q3 paydays, July 10 to September 18. Every federal tax deposit for the quarter went through EFTPS.

Omar Rasmussen gave payroll a WA Cares exemption approval in July, and payroll stopped that deduction from the July 24 payday.

Tomas Arvelo is paid through accounts payable, not payroll, for concrete finishing at Tideflats Cold Storage.

Two more employees say WA Cares exemption applications have been sent in. No approval letter has arrived for either application, so payroll still takes the WA Cares deduction from both employees' paychecks.

The other records are in the client folder: the employer accounts, the Q1 and Q2 returns as filed, the 2026 rate records, the employee roster, the exemption approvals on file, the payroll ledger accounts and the labor vendors paid.

Dana Whitfield
Controller, HANGS Construction Services LLC

messages.subject: HANGS Construction Services Q3 2026 payroll reports
messages.body:
Hello,

Please prepare the Q3 2026 payroll reports for HANGS Construction Services LLC: Form 941, the ESD unemployment insurance tax and wage report, the Paid Leave and WA Cares report, and the L&I workers' compensation quarterly report. Each report is a draft for review; nothing is filed or paid until the review is done.

Attached are the Q3 2026 payroll register, the federal tax deposit log and the Q2 2026 year-to-date wages by employee. The register is the final export from the payroll system for the six Q3 paydays, July 10 to September 18. Every federal tax deposit for the quarter went through EFTPS.

Omar Rasmussen gave payroll a WA Cares exemption approval in July, and payroll stopped that deduction from the July 24 payday.

Tomas Arvelo is paid through accounts payable, not payroll, for concrete finishing at Tideflats Cold Storage.

Two more employees say WA Cares exemption applications have been sent in. No approval letter has arrived for either application, so payroll still takes the WA Cares deduction from both employees' paychecks.

The other records are in the client folder: the employer accounts, the Q1 and Q2 returns as filed, the 2026 rate records, the employee roster, the exemption approvals on file, the payroll ledger accounts and the labor vendors paid.

Dana Whitfield
Controller, HANGS Construction Services LLC
payroll@hangs-gc.example

sources.title: Washington workers' comp insurance average premium will rise about 4.9% in 2026 (news release 25-32)
sources.issuer: Washington State Department of Labor & Industries

passages.q: When did the 2026 rates start, and what is the premium measured on?
passages.a: The average cost of workers' compensation insurance in Washington for 2026 will go up 4.9 percent ... Starting Jan. 1, employers and workers together will pay, on average, $1.37 a week more for each full-time position. ... The 4.9 percent increase is an average for all industries. ... Washington's workers' compensation premiums are based on hours worked by the worker. When wages go up in Washington, employer and worker contributions stay the same.

sources.title: Employers' Guide to Workers' Compensation Insurance in Washington State (F101-002-000)
sources.issuer: Washington State Department of Labor & Industries

passages.q: Can a worker's hours be divided between two classes, and on what records?
passages.a: The worker hours of any one employee may be divided for reporting purposes between two or more assigned basic risk classifications. This may be done only when accurate records of actual hours worked, supported by original timecard or time-book entries, document the division of duties. You may not divide a worker's hours between a "basic" classification and a "standard exception" classification ... If you do not keep accurate records of divided worker hours, all of a worker's hours must be reported in the highest rated classification in which the worker has duties. Estimates or percentages are not acceptable documentation for splitting hours.

passages.q: How much may payroll withhold from workers, and on which hours?
passages.a: The Supplemental-Pension assessment is not experience rated. ... a portion of the premium due, equal to one-half of the Medical Aid Fund rate, Stay at Work rate, and Supplemental Pension Fund assessment, may be paid by employee contribution. ... It is illegal to withhold more than the authorized amount. Each pay period, calculate the amount you withhold by multiplying the payroll deduction rate ... times the actual number of hours/units each employee worked. ... Do not include sick leave hours, vacations or holidays, even if it is paid leave. ... each hour of overtime work is reported as one hour, even though time-and-a-half wages may have been paid.

sources.title: Workers' Compensation Recordkeeping and Reporting Guides (F212-222-000)
sources.issuer: Washington State Department of Labor & Industries

passages.q: In which class does the Safety Manager, coded 4904 but working at the office and job sites, belong?
passages.a: A division of a single worker's hours SHALL NOT be permitted between two standard exception classifications or between a standard exception classification and a basic business classification. Clerical Office - Class 4904 workers are defined as those individuals whose duties are confined to keeping the books or records of the employer, in or about the employer's premises. ... If any worker described above is exposed to any operative hazard of the business, their entire worker hours shall be assigned to the highest rated classification of work to which they are exposed.

passages.q: Which hours count for hourly and salaried workers, and which records support those hours?
passages.a: Computing Worker Hours. Hourly Workers: Workers who receive an hourly wage. Actual hours. Includes overtime. Excludes holiday, vacation, and sick pay. Salaried Workers: Workers who receive a fixed wage each pay period. 160 hours per month = 480 hours per quarter or Actual hours. The same method must be used for all salaried workers. ... Time Record showing days worked and hours worked each day ... Daily and summary time records must show the applicable occupation and risk class.

sources.issuer: Washington State Department of Labor & Industries

passages.q: Which hours belong in Q3 when a pay period crosses the quarter end?
passages.a: Enter your workers' actual hours, even if there were zero, within the correct risk classes for the quarter that just ended. ... Quarter three (July - Sept.) Oct. 31

sources.issuer: Washington State Department of Labor & Industries

passages.q: When were the Q3 2026 report and premium due?
passages.a: Quarterly reports and premiums are due 4 times per year: ... 3 | July 1 - September 30 | October 31 ... Weekend due dates may be postmarked the following business day.

sources.title: Penalties and Interest for Filing Late
sources.issuer: Washington State Department of Labor & Industries

passages.q: What does L&I charge when the report or premium is late?
passages.a: We assess this penalty and charge interest when you are late filing your quarterly report or have unpaid workers' compensation premiums. ... No penalty amount will be less than $10 ... 1: Total of 5% of the premium due, 1% interest on the premium due. 2: Total of 10% of the premium due, 2% interest on the premium due. 3: Total of 20% of the premium due, 3% interest on the premium due. 4+: Additional 1% interest each month until the premium is paid.

sources.title: RCW 51.08.181, Worker: registered contractor and electrician exclusions

passages.q: Is Tomas Arvelo, paid as a vendor for concrete finishing, outside workers' compensation coverage?
passages.a: For the purposes of this title, any individual performing services that require registration under chapter 18.27 RCW or licensing under chapter 18.106 or 19.28 RCW for remuneration under an independent contract is not a worker when: (1) The individual has been, and will continue to be, free from control or direction over the performance of the service, both under the contract of service and in fact; ... (5) ... and has registered for and received a unified business identifier number from the state of Washington; ... and (7) On the effective date of the contract of service, the individual has a valid contractor registration pursuant to chapter 18.27 RCW ...

sources.title: RCW 51.16.060, Quarterly report of payrolls

passages.q: What must the quarterly report give L&I, and when does an unpaid premium become delinquent?
passages.a: ... shall, on or before the last day of January, April, July and October of each year thereafter, furnish the department with a true and accurate payroll for the period in which workers were employed by it during the preceding calendar quarter, the total amount paid to such workers during such preceding calendar quarter, and a segregation of employment in the different classes established pursuant to this title ... Premiums for a calendar quarter, whether reported or not, shall become due and delinquent on the day immediately following the last day of the month following the calendar quarter.

sources.title: RCW 51.16.140, Premium liability of worker

passages.q: Which part of the premium does the statute let an employer take from wages?
passages.a: (1) Every employer who is not a self-insurer shall deduct from the pay of each of his or her workers one-half of the amount he or she is required to pay, for medical benefits within each risk classification. ... (2) It shall be unlawful for the employer, unless specifically authorized by this title, to deduct or obtain any part of the premium or other costs required to be by him or her paid from the wages or earnings of any of his or her workers, and the making of or attempt to make any such deduction shall be a gross misdemeanor.

sources.title: RCW 51.32.073, Premium liability of worker and employer for additional payments (supplemental pension)

passages.q: Who pays the supplemental pension part of the rate?
passages.a: (1) Except as provided in subsection (2) of this section, each employer shall retain from the earnings of each worker that amount as shall be fixed from time to time by the director, the basis for measuring said amount to be determined by the director. The money so retained shall be matched in an equal amount by each employer, and all such moneys shall be remitted to the department in such manner and at such intervals as the department directs and shall be placed in the supplemental pension fund

sources.title: RCW 51.48.210, Delinquent taxes

passages.q: How does the statute count a late month, and what is the minimum penalty and the interest?
passages.a: If payment of any tax due is not received by the department by the due date, there shall be assessed a penalty of five percent of the amount of the tax for the first month or part thereof of delinquency; there shall be assessed a total penalty of ten percent of the amount of the tax for the second month or part thereof of delinquency; and there shall be assessed a total penalty of twenty percent of the amount of the tax for the third month or part thereof of delinquency. No penalty so added may be less than ten dollars. ... delinquent taxes shall bear interest at the rate of one percent of the delinquent amount per month or fraction thereof from and after the due date until payment ...

sources.title: WAC 296-17-31021, Units of exposure

passages.q: How are salaried employees' hours reported?
passages.a: For most businesses the unit of exposure is the hours worked by their employees. ... Salaried employees: You must select one of the following methods to report your salaried employees: Actual hours worked; or Assumed hours of one hundred-sixty hours per month. All salaried employees of an employer must be reported by the same method. You cannot report some salaried employees based on the actual hours they work and others using the one hundred sixty hours per month method.

sources.title: WAC 296-17-31024, Classification premium rates

passages.q: How is each class's hourly rate for HANGS Construction Services built from the base rates?
passages.a: You are charged premiums using base rates for each of your risk classifications. ... Your premiums for each classification are determined by multiplying your experience factor by the sum of the accident fund, medical aid fund and stay-at-work program base rates for that class, and then adding the supplemental pension fund rate.

sources.title: WAC 296-17-920, Assessment for supplemental pension fund

passages.q: How much supplemental pension may be retained from each worker in 2026?
passages.a: The amount of 95.6 mils ($0.0956) shall be retained by each employer from the earnings of each worker for each hour or fraction thereof the worker is employed. The amount of money so retained from the employee shall be matched in an equal amount by each employer ... WSR 25-24-041, filed 11/26/25, effective 1/1/26

sources.title: WAC 296-17A-0217, Classification 0217 (concrete flatwork)

passages.q: Does the Rainier Commons concrete package belong in 0217?
passages.a: 0217-00 Concrete flatwork - Construction and/or repair: N.O.C. Applies to: Contractors engaged in the construction and/or repair of concrete flatwork not covered by another classification (N.O.C.). ... Pouring and finishing of concrete; ... Exclusions: ... Concrete work contained within a building or structure made of concrete, masonry, iron or steel frame, such as the foundation, floor slab, precast or poured in place bearing floors or wall panels, columns, pillars, metal erection or any other portion of the building or structure itself, is classified in 0518; ... Concrete work performed on or in connection with projects on highways, streets, or roadways ... is classified in 0214

passages.q: Which Q3 jobs belong in 0510, wood frame building construction?
passages.a: 0510-00 Wood frame building: Construction or alterations, N.O.C. ... For the purposes of this classification, wood frame building construction means buildings erected exclusively of wood or wood products. This classification includes all building framing activities done in connection with wood frame building construction ... Constructing a new wood frame building that never existed - 0510;

passages.q: Which Q3 jobs belong in 0518, non-wood frame buildings?
passages.a: 0518-00 Nonwood frame buildings and structures, new construction and repair, N.O.C. Applies to work on nonwood frame buildings and structures ... when the superstructure (skeleton framework or building shell) consists of concrete, iron or steel, or a combination of concrete, iron, steel and/or wood ... Pouring and finishing concrete within the building or structure such as: ... Precast or poured in place load bearing floors or wall panels; ... The raising and/or standing up (by crane or boom) of concrete: Tilt-up walls; ... Metal frames. ... Note: The installation of exterior doors, door frames, all interior framing, and other interior rough-in carpentry work is reported separately in classi

sources.title: WAC 296-17A-4900, Classification 4900 (construction superintendent or project manager)

passages.q: Which superintendents and project managers belong in 4900?
passages.a: 4900-00 Construction: Superintendent or project manager. Applies to employees with administrative oversight or management duties who visit or work at construction sites but who do not directly take part in any construction operations. ... Inspection of work. This classification excludes anyone at a construction site who: Directly supervises the work of employees or independent contractors; Performs manual labor; Operates or repairs equipment; Delivers supplies or equipment. If superintendents or project managers perform any excluded duties, then all of their hours for that project must be reported in the construction classification(s) applicable to the work they perform. If detailed records

sources.title: WAC 296-17A-4904, Classification 4904 (clerical office)

passages.q: Who belongs in 4904 Clerical Office?
passages.a: 4904-00 Clerical office, N.O.C. Clerical office employees whose job duties and work environment meet all the conditions of the general reporting rules covering clerical office standard exception employees ... Care must be taken to look beyond job titles ... Work environment is restricted to a business office, meeting room, or similar office-like environment that is: Physically separated by walls, partitions, or other physical barriers from all other work areas ... Classification 4904 permits limited and minimal work outside an office for: Attending meetings; Banking; Purchasing supplies for the office; Taking correspondence to or from the post office; Taking training courses.

sources.title: WAC 296-17A-4911, Classification 4911 (construction estimators)

passages.q: Do the estimators belong in 4911?
passages.a: 4911-00 Construction estimators. Applies to: Employees of construction or erection contractors who work as cost and materials estimators preparing bids for contracts away from their employer's business offices. ... Notes: This classification is restricted in that employees reported in it cannot have any other duties other than construction estimating during their work shift or work day. Any employee working as an estimator and having any construction-related duties during the same work shift or day is to be reported separately in the applicable construction or erection classification for that entire work shift.
